title: Add `validate_sparse` keyword to `torch.load`
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.12.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #184750

Loading a sparse tensor on a `weights_only=True` checkpoint previously fell back to the global `torch.sparse.check_sparse_tensor_invariants` setting, which defaults off. With invariants unchecked, a malformed checkpoint can produce a sparse tensor whose indices point outside the dense shape, causing out-of-bounds reads (e.g. in `to_dense`) once the loaded object is used.

`torch.load` now accepts `validate_sparse: Optional[bool] = None`. `True` always runs the invariant check (overriding the global setting), `False` skips it, and `None` defers to the global setting except in `weights_only=True` mode where it raises and asks the caller to choose explicitly. The check itself is O(nnz) per sparse tensor, so the keyword lets callers trade safety against load time without flipping a global.

`_validate_loaded_sparse_tensors` is restructured around a single `try/finally` so `_sparse_tensors_to_validate` is always cleared regardless of which early-exit path is taken.

The existing `test_skip_data_serialization_*` cases now pass `validate_sparse=False` because `skip_data` leaves storage uninitialized; the save-side flag is not observable at load time so the caller has to opt out explicitly.

Authored by Claude.
